Have you ever felt that deep longing for real connection, or wondered what it truly means to belong somewhere? You're not alone. That search for purpose and a sense of home is something we all share—no matter where we come from or how fast the world is changing around us. Even as technology pushes us further apart, that ancient pull toward togetherness is as strong as ever.
Together, let's step into the world of Tribe: On Homecoming and Belonging by Sebastian Junger. This is more than just a book—it's an invitation to explore why we crave community, and how facing challenges side by side can unite us in ways comfort and abundance never could. Through stories drawn from history, anthropology, and personal experience, we'll discover how our most primal instincts shape the way we respond to war, disaster, and even the loneliness that sometimes comes with modern life. We'll meet indigenous cultures and modern veterans, and see why hardship so often brings people together, while too much ease can leave us feeling isolated. There's this fascinating tension between wanting to be free as individuals, and needing to lean on one another as a community. So, what does it really mean to come home—not just to a place, but to a feeling of true belonging? As we explore these questions, get ready to reflect on your own journey, and maybe even find new ways to connect—with yourself, and with the world around you.
